ambiguities_or_notes: Audit and retranslation of the christisinourhearts.com English text (version 1.0, 29 September 2026). Every Russian paragraph was aligned with the website paragraphs (through the site's English-Russian parallel edition) and checked source-forward; the website text served as a first draft and was revised wherever it departed from the Russian.

Mechanical alignment: 49/49 page markers in identical sequence and at the same paragraph positions (44 inside paragraphs, 5 as separate blocks); title, two part headings, 23 + 20 chapter headings; 565/565 source paragraphs mapped one-to-one; footnotes [^1]–[^4] at the same places, with the edition's four translations of Tolstoy's French rendered in the Notes. The website splits the Russian paragraphs into 1,017 display paragraphs (dialogue lines with speaker labels); the repository keeps the Russian paragraphing.

About 300 English corrections were classed as hard fidelity defects in the revision pass (omissions, additions, wrong meanings, referents and speakers, softened or intensified statements, names). Examples: I ch. II «валить?» was 'Shall we do it?' (Makhin asks whether he should go ahead) and «Как же...» was 'Of course...'; I ch. IX the unquoted «Будь с ними хорош, и они будут хороши» had been made a quotation with a different meaning; I ch. XV the Tsar 'who alone pitied the people and was just' had become one he 'still believed' to be just; I ch. XVI the 'lame, legless tailor' had been softened to one 'who had difficulty walking'; I ch. XXI Turchaninova asks for a visit (свидание) with Tyurin, not to be received by the minister; I ch. XXII and II ch. XIV the French had been translated into the body with 'in French' added; II ch. III Stepan's reasoning on the Gospel (the merciful to paradise, the unmerciful to hell) and both Gospel references had been cut; II ch. VII Makhin's account had lost 'converted the executioner', the reason he remembers, and 'he did not enter Stepan's soul'; II ch. IX the escape scene had been compressed by about a dozen sentences; II ch. XI the telegram scene had turned reported speech into dialogue; II ch. XIV «что дальше, то хуже» had become 'the more direct he became'; II ch. XVI an invented 'how Maria Semyonovna had changed him'.

Names: Fyodor (not Fedor), Yeropkin(a), the Liventsovs (not Livenzov); Pyotr Nikolaich where Tolstoy writes Николаич and Pyotr Nikolayevich where he writes Николаевич (I ch. IX opening, the telegram).

Terms held: купон 'coupon'; гимназист 'schoolboy'; становой 'district police officer'; земский начальник 'land captain' (the site had 'zemstvo chief'); урядник 'sergeant'; смотритель 'governor'; царь 'Tsar' and государь 'Sovereign' (the site mixed 'Emperor'); старец 'elder' (not 'old monk'); цыган 'Gypsy' (the site had 'Roma' and 'Romani'; choice for Andrei); Разве можно? 'How can you do such a thing?' in I ch. XXIII and its echo in II ch. I; простить 'forgive' kept apart from помиловать 'pardon'; Отче наш 'the Our Father'.

Kept as Tolstoy wrote it: historic present in II ch. IX; free indirect speech (I ch. IX, II ch. XIII); Vasily's misspelled letter (II ch. XVII) marked lightly; the French in French; the archimandrite inconsistency (I ch. XVIII, XX).

Process: eleven same-model subagents revised the chapters source-forward (English and Romanian together) from aligned packets; then four fresh-session subagents audited the English against the Russian, source-forward and reverse (independence: fresh-session, same model family). They found 1 hard defect (земский начальник as 'zemstvo chief', now 'land captain', applied in all three places) and 25 soft points, 24 adopted (one number-style point declined). One reversed sentence order (I ch. IX «Это что?») was corrected by merging two website paragraphs. This is not an other-model or human verification.
